4. Idle cash earns 0 (no interest, no inflation adjustment).

---

### Optimal value
$$
W^\star \;=\; 510{,}000 \text{ yuan.}
$$

Because $1.7\times 3 = 3\times 1.7 = 5.1$, any sequence that fills the 3-year horizon with one 1-year and one 2-year leg yields the same final wealth. Two corner-point optima are:

| $t$ | $x_1[t]$ | $x_2[t]$ | $s[t]$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 100,000 | 100,000 |
| 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 300,000 | — | 0 |
| 4 | — | — | 0 |

Cash trace: $100{,}000 \xrightarrow{\times 3} 300{,}000 \xrightarrow{\times 1.7} 510{,}000$.

**Strategy B — "1-year first, then 2-year":**

| $t$ | $x_1[t]$ | $x_2[t]$ | $s[t]$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 100,000 | 0 | 100,000 |
| 2 | 0 | 170,000 | 0 |
| 3 | 0 | — | 0 |
| 4 | — | — | 0 |

Cash trace: $100{,}000 \xrightarrow{\times 1.7} 170{,}000 \xrightarrow{\times 3} 510{,}000$.

**Strategy C (any convex combination):** pick any $\alpha\in[0,1]$ and set
$x_1[1]=100{,}000\,\alpha,\; x_2[1]=100{,}000\,(1-\alpha),\; x_2[2]=170{,}000\,\alpha,\; x_1[3]=300{,}000\,(1-\alpha)$, all other variables 0. Final wealth is always $5.1\cdot 100{,}000=510{,}000$.

---

## 3. LP / Dual Argument for Optimality

Let $\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_3$ be the dual multipliers of (C1)–(C3). The dual is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min\;& 100{,}000\,\pi_1\\
\text{s.t. }& \pi_1 - 1.7\pi_2 \ge 0 &&(x_1[1])\\
& \pi_1 - 3\pi_3 \ge 0 &&(x_2[1])\\
& \pi_1 - \pi_2 \ge 0 &&(s[2])\\
& \pi_2 - 1.7\pi_3 \ge 0 &&(x_1[2])\\
& \pi_2 \ge 3 &&(x_2[2])\\
& \pi_2 - \pi_3 \ge 0 &&(s[3])\\
& \pi_3 \ge 1.7 &&(x_1[3])\\
& \pi_3 \ge 1 &&(s[4]).
\end{aligned}
$$

Tightening the binding constraints $\pi_2\ge 3$ and $\pi_3\ge 1.7$ forces
$\pi_1 \ge 1.7\pi_2 = 5.1$ and $\pi_1 \ge 3\pi_3 = 5.1$. The minimum is

$$
\boxed{\;\pi_1^\star = 5.1,\quad \pi_2^\star = 3,\quad \pi_3^\star = 1.7\;}
$$

giving dual objective $100{,}000\times 5.1 = 510{,}000$. By strong LP duality, $W^\star = 510{,}000$.

**Economic reading of the duals (shadow prices of cash at the beginning of each year):**
- $\pi_3^\star = 1.7$: one extra yuan at $t=3$ is worth $1.7$ yuan at $t=4$ (use the 1-year option).
- $\pi_2^\star = 3$: one extra yuan at $t=2$ is worth $3$ yuan at $t=4$ (use the 2-year option).
- $\pi_1^\star = 5.1$: one extra yuan at $t=1$ is worth $5.1$ yuan at $t=4$ (combine the two options over the 3-year horizon).

**Complementary slackness** confirms the structure of the optimal set: $\pi_1-\pi_2=2.1>0 \Rightarrow s[2]=0$; $\pi_2-\pi_3=1.3>0 \Rightarrow s[3]=0$; $\pi_3-1=0.7>0 \Rightarrow s[4]=0$; $\pi_2-1.7\pi_3=0.11>0 \Rightarrow x_1[2]=0$. The remaining primal variables $x_1[1],x_2[1],x_2[2],x_1[3]$ are free to vary along the face $x_1[1]+x_2[1]=100{,}000,\; x_2[2]=1.7\,x_1[1],\; x_1[3]=3\,x_2[1]$, which is exactly the family of optima described above.

---

## 4. Bottom Line

- The corrected MILP has 8 continuous variables, 2 binaries (redundant), 3 equality constraints, and 2 big-M linking constraints.
- **Optimal final wealth: $W^\star = 510{,}000$ yuan** (a $5.1\times$ return on the initial $100{,}000$).

response.content:
# Linear Model: Two-Option Investment over a 3-Year Horizon

---

## 1. Problem Data, Timeline and Notation

| Item | Symbol | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Initial capital (available at start of Year 1) | $W_0$ | $100{,}000$ yuan |
| Horizon | — | end of Year 3 |
| Option 1 ("1‑yr"): profit per yuan invested, paid 1 year later | $r_1$ | $0.7$ → 1 yuan becomes $1.7$ |
| Option 2 ("2‑yr"): profit per yuan invested, paid 2 years later | $r_2$ | $2$ → 1 yuan becomes $3$ |
| Holding period of Option 2 | — | must be a multiple of 2 years |

**Timeline (decision points = beginnings of years):**

```
t=1 (Begin Yr 1)      t=2 (Begin Yr 2)      t=3 (Begin Yr 3)      t=4 (End Yr 3)
   |-------------------------|---------------------|---------------------|
   x1[1], x2[1]              x1[2], x2[2]            x1[3]                (terminal)
        |                        |                     |
   Option1 matures t=2      Option1 matures t=3   Option1 matures t=4
   Option2 matures t=3      Option2 matures t=4   (Option2 at t=3 → matures t=5: INFEASIBLE)
```

**Index sets**
- $T_1=\{1,2,3\}$ — beginnings of years in which Option 1 may be started (all three years are feasible).
- $T_2=\{1,2\}$ — beginnings of years in which Option 2 may be started (starting at $t=3$ would mature at $t=5$, beyond the horizon).
- $T=\{1,2,3,4\}$ — cash states; $t=4$ is the terminal date.

## 2. Assumptions

1. **Guaranteed, deterministic returns.** Option 1 pays exactly $0.7$ per yuan after exactly 1 year; Option 2 pays exactly $2$ per yuan after exactly 2 years. No risk, no uncertainty.
2. **No early redemption.** Proceeds of an investment are received *exactly* at its maturity date and cannot be withdrawn earlier.
3. **Divisibility.** Capital is perfectly divisible; the yuan-integer restriction is relaxed to continuous variables. This is harmless here because the optimal solution uses round amounts ($100{,}000$, $300{,}000$).
4. **Idle cash earns 0%.** Any uninvested cash is simply held (no interest, no inflation adjustment).
5. **No transaction costs, no minimum ticket, no fixed fee.** Capital can be split arbitrarily among the two options and idle cash at any decision point.
6. **Reinvestment is allowed.** Matured funds become available for new investments at the next decision point.
7. **No investment beyond the horizon** (money cannot be left in an instrument maturing after $t=4$).
8. **Principal is returned in full** at maturity together with the profit (so Option 1 returns $1.7$ per yuan, Option 2 returns $3$ per yuan).

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Meaning | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $x_1[t]$ | yuan placed in Option 1 at the beginning of year $t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0},\ t\in T_1$ |
| $x_2[t]$ | yuan placed in Option 2 at the beginning of year $t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0},\ t\in T_2$ |
| $s[t]$ | idle cash carried into the beginning of year $t$ ($s[1]=W_0$; $s[4]$ = cash held at the end of Year 3) | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0},\ t\in T$ |
| $y[t]$ | 1 if Option 2 is started at the beginning of year $t$, else 0 | $\{0,1\},\ t\in T_2$ |

## 4. Objective Function

Maximize the total wealth (principal + profit) in hand at the end of Year 3. Using maturity cash flows (principal **and** profit):

$$\max \quad W \;=\; s[4] \;+\; 1.7\,x_1[3] \;+\; 3\,x_2[2]$$

**Equivalent objective (profit form).** Because all principal is returned at maturity, substituting the balance equations into $W$ gives the identity

$$W \;=\; W_0 \;+\; 0.7\big(x_1[1]+x_1[2]+x_1[3]\big) \;+\; 2\big(x_2[1]+x_2[2]\big)$$

so one may equivalently write $\max \ \pi = 0.7\sum_{t\in T_1}x_1[t] + 2\sum_{t\in T_2}x_2[t]$ (total profit), with $W^\star = 100{,}000+\pi^\star$.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Cash balance at the beginning of Year 1** (initial capital $W_0$):

$$x_1[1] + x_2[1] + s[2] = 100{,}000$$

**(C2) Cash balance at the beginning of Year 2** (Option 1 started in Year 1 matures with profit $0.7\,x_1[1]$):

$$x_1[2] + x_2[2] + s[3] = s[2] + 1.7\,x_1[1]$$

**(C3) Cash balance at the beginning of Year 3** (Option 1 started in Year 2 matures; Option 2 started in Year 1 matures with $3\,x_2[1]$):

$$x_1[3] + s[4] = s[3] + 1.7\,x_1[2] + 3\,x_2[1]$$

**(C4) Initial cash state:** $s[1] = 100{,}000$ (subsumed in C1; stated for clarity).

**(C5) Linking / big‑M constraints (MILP form only):**

$$x_2[1] \le M_1\,y[1], \qquad x_2[2] \le M_2\,y[2]$$

with **tight** big‑M values: $M_1 = 100{,}000$ (cash at $t=1$ is exactly $100{,}000$) and $M_2 = 170{,}000$ (at most $1.7\times100{,}000=170{,}000$ can ever be available at $t=2$, attained by putting everything in Option 1 in Year 1).

**(C6) Domains:** $x_1[t],x_2[t],s[t]\ge 0$; $y[t]\in\{0,1\}$.

> **Note (LP vs. MILP).** Under Assumption 5 there is no fixed fee or minimum ticket for opening Option 2, so the binaries $y[t]$ are **provably redundant**: whenever $x_2[t]>0$ one sets $y[t]=1$, and C5 is never binding at an optimum. The problem as stated is therefore a **pure linear program** (the MILP above is needed only if a minimum investment size or an opening fee is introduced).

## 6. Optimal Solution

$$\boxed{W^\star = 510{,}000 \ \text{yuan}\qquad(\pi^\star = 410{,}000\ \text{yuan profit, a } 5.1\times \text{return})}$$

### Recommended plan — "2‑year option first, then 1‑year option"

| Decision point | $x_1[t]$ (1‑yr) | $x_2[t]$ (2‑yr) | $s[t]$ (idle) | Cash available |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Begin Year 1 | 0 | **100,000** | 0 | 100,000 |
| Begin Year 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | $3\times100{,}000=300{,}000$ |
| Begin Year 3 | **300,000** | — | 0 | 300,000 |
| End Year 3 | — | — | 0 | **510,000** |

Cash trace: $100{,}000 \xrightarrow{\times 3} 300{,}000 \xrightarrow{\times 1.7} 510{,}000$.

### The continuum of optimal strategies

The LP has a whole face of optima. Let $a\in[0,100{,}000]$:

$$x_1[1]=a,\quad x_2[1]=100{,}000-a,\quad x_2[2]=1.7a,\quad x_1[3]=3(100{,}000-a),\quad x_1[2]=s[2]=s[3]=s[4]=0$$

For every $a$ this yields $W = 5.1(100{,}000-a)+5.1a = 510{,}000$. Two extreme points:

| $a$ | Plan | Final wealth |
|---|---|---|
| $a=0$ | All 100,000 → Option 2 in Yr 1; 300,000 → Option 1 in Yr 3 | 510,000 |
| $a=100{,}000$ | All 100,000 → Option 1 in Yr 1; 170,000 → Option 2 in Yr 2 | 510,000 |

## 7. Optimality Certificate

**(a) Dominance argument.** Value per yuan available with $k$ years remaining, $g(k)$: $g(1)=1.7$; $g(2)=\max\{1.7^2,\,3\}=3$; $g(3)=\max\{1.7^3,\,1.7\cdot3,\,3\cdot1.7\}=5.1$. Since $5.1 > 4.913 = 1.7^3$ and $5.1 > 3$, no strategy can beat $5.1$ per yuan, so $W\le 100{,}000\times5.1=510{,}000$ — attained above.

**(b) LP dual.** With multipliers $\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_3$ on (C1)–(C3):

$$\min\; 100{,}000\,\pi_1 \quad \text{s.t. } \begin{aligned}
\pi_1 - 1.7\pi_2 &\ge 0 & (x_1[1])\\
\pi_1 - 3\pi_3 &\ge 0 & (x_2[1])\\
\pi_1 - \pi_2 &\ge 0 & (s[2])\\
\pi_2 - 1.7\pi_3 &\ge 0 & (x_1[2])\\
\pi_2 &\ge 3 & (x_2[2])\\
\pi_2 - \pi_3 &\ge 0 & (s[3])\\
\pi_3 &\ge 1.7 & (x_1[3])\\
\pi_3 &\ge 1 & (s[4])
\end{aligned}$$

The feasible dual point $\pi^*=(5.1,\;3,\;1.7)$ has objective $100{,}000\times5.1=510{,}000$, which equals the primal value — by strong duality the plan is optimal. *Economic reading of the duals:* one extra yuan at the beginning of Year 3 is worth 1.7 yuan at the end (use Option 1); at the beginning of Year 2 it is worth 3 yuan (use Option 2); at the beginning of Year 1 it is worth 5.1 yuan (use both options). Complementary slackness confirms $s[2]=s[3]=s[4]=x_1[2]=0$ at any optimum and leaves the free face parameterized by $a$ above.

## 8. Recommendation

**Invest the entire 100,000 yuan in the 2‑year option at the beginning of Year 1.** It matures at the end of Year 2 for 300,000 yuan; invest that entire 300,000 in the 1‑year option at the beginning of Year 3, which matures at the end of Year 3 for **510,000 yuan** (profit 410,000 yuan ≈ 4.1× the initial capital, ≈ 72.6 % p.a. compounded). The order may be reversed (1‑year first, then 2‑year) with identical results — the key is to fill the 3‑year horizon with exactly one 1‑year leg and one 2‑year leg, since $1.7\times3=5.1$ beats any other feasible combination.

# Linear Model: Two-Option Investment over a 3-Year Horizon

---

## 1. Problem Data, Timeline and Notation

| Item | Symbol | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Initial capital (available at start of Year 1) | $W_0$ | $100{,}000$ yuan |
| Horizon | — | end of Year 3 |
| Option 1 ("1‑yr"): profit per yuan invested, paid 1 year later | $r_1$ | $0.7$ → 1 yuan becomes $1.7$ |
| Option 2 ("2‑yr"): profit per yuan invested, paid 2 years later | $r_2$ | $2$ → 1 yuan becomes $3$ |
| Holding period of Option 2 | — | must be a multiple of 2 years |

**Timeline (decision points = beginnings of years):**

```
t=1 (Begin Yr 1)      t=2 (Begin Yr 2)      t=3 (Begin Yr 3)      t=4 (End Yr 3)
   |-------------------------|---------------------|---------------------|
   x1[1], x2[1]              x1[2], x2[2]            x1[3]                (terminal)
        |                        |                     |
   Option1 matures t=2      Option1 matures t=3   Option1 matures t=4
   Option2 matures t=3      Option2 matures t=4   (Option2 at t=3 → matures t=5: INFEASIBLE)
```

**Index sets**
- $T_1=\{1,2,3\}$ — beginnings of years in which Option 1 may be started (all three years are feasible).
- $T_2=\{1,2\}$ — beginnings of years in which Option 2 may be started (starting at $t=3$ would mature at $t=5$, beyond the horizon).
- $T=\{1,2,3,4\}$ — cash states; $t=4$ is the terminal date.

## 2. Assumptions

1. **Guaranteed, deterministic returns.** Option 1 pays exactly $0.7$ per yuan after exactly 1 year; Option 2 pays exactly $2$ per yuan after exactly 2 years. No risk, no uncertainty.
2. **No early redemption.** Proceeds of an investment are received *exactly* at its maturity date and cannot be withdrawn earlier.
3. **Divisibility.** Capital is perfectly divisible; the yuan-integer restriction is relaxed to continuous variables. This is harmless here because the optimal solution uses round amounts ($100{,}000$, $300{,}000$).
4. **Idle cash earns 0%.** Any uninvested cash is simply held (no interest, no inflation adjustment).
5. **No transaction costs, no minimum ticket, no fixed fee.** Capital can be split arbitrarily among the two options and idle cash at any decision point.
6. **Reinvestment is allowed.** Matured funds become available for new investments at the next decision point.
7. **No investment beyond the horizon** (money cannot be left in an instrument maturing after $t=4$).
8. **Principal is returned in full** at maturity together with the profit (so Option 1 returns $1.7$ per yuan, Option 2 returns $3$ per yuan).

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Meaning | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| $x_1[t]$ | yuan placed in Option 1 at the beginning of year $t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0},\ t\in T_1$ |
| $x_2[t]$ | yuan placed in Option 2 at the beginning of year $t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0},\ t\in T_2$ |
| $s[t]$ | idle cash carried into the beginning of year $t$ ($s[1]=W_0$; $s[4]$ = cash held at the end of Year 3) | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0},\ t\in T$ |
| $y[t]$ | 1 if Option 2 is started at the beginning of year $t$, else 0 | $\{0,1\},\ t\in T_2$ |

## 4. Objective Function

Maximize the total wealth (principal + profit) in hand at the end of Year 3. Using maturity cash flows (principal **and** profit):

$$\max \quad W \;=\; s[4] \;+\; 1.7\,x_1[3] \;+\; 3\,x_2[2]$$

**Equivalent objective (profit form).** Because all principal is returned at maturity, substituting the balance equations into $W$ gives the identity

$$W \;=\; W_0 \;+\; 0.7\big(x_1[1]+x_1[2]+x_1[3]\big) \;+\; 2\big(x_2[1]+x_2[2]\big)$$

so one may equivalently write $\max \ \pi = 0.7\sum_{t\in T_1}x_1[t] + 2\sum_{t\in T_2}x_2[t]$ (total profit), with $W^\star = 100{,}000+\pi^\star$.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Cash balance at the beginning of Year 1** (initial capital $W_0$):

$$x_1[1] + x_2[1] + s[2] = 100{,}000$$

**(C2) Cash balance at the beginning of Year 2** (Option 1 started in Year 1 matures with profit $0.7\,x_1[1]$):

$$x_1[2] + x_2[2] + s[3] = s[2] + 1.7\,x_1[1]$$

**(C3) Cash balance at the beginning of Year 3** (Option 1 started in Year 2 matures; Option 2 started in Year 1 matures with $3\,x_2[1]$):

$$x_1[3] + s[4] = s[3] + 1.7\,x_1[2] + 3\,x_2[1]$$

**(C4) Initial cash state:** $s[1] = 100{,}000$ (subsumed in C1; stated for clarity).

**(C5) Linking / big‑M constraints (MILP form only):**

$$x_2[1] \le M_1\,y[1], \qquad x_2[2] \le M_2\,y[2]$$

with **tight** big‑M values: $M_1 = 100{,}000$ (cash at $t=1$ is exactly $100{,}000$) and $M_2 = 170{,}000$ (at most $1.7\times100{,}000=170{,}000$ can ever be available at $t=2$, attained by putting everything in Option 1 in Year 1).

**(C6) Domains:** $x_1[t],x_2[t],s[t]\ge 0$; $y[t]\in\{0,1\}$.

> **Note (LP vs. MILP).** Under Assumption 5 there is no fixed fee or minimum ticket for opening Option 2, so the binaries $y[t]$ are **provably redundant**: whenever $x_2[t]>0$ one sets $y[t]=1$, and C5 is never binding at an optimum. The problem as stated is therefore a **pure linear program** (the MILP above is needed only if a minimum investment size or an opening fee is introduced).

## 6. Optimal Solution

$$\boxed{W^\star = 510{,}000 \ \text{yuan}\qquad(\pi^\star = 410{,}000\ \text{yuan profit, a } 5.1\times \text{return})}$$

### Recommended plan — "2‑year option first, then 1‑year option"

| Decision point | $x_1[t]$ (1‑yr) | $x_2[t]$ (2‑yr) | $s[t]$ (idle) | Cash available |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Begin Year 1 | 0 | **100,000** | 0 | 100,000 |
| Begin Year 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | $3\times100{,}000=300{,}000$ |
| Begin Year 3 | **300,000** | — | 0 | 300,000 |
| End Year 3 | — | — | 0 | **510,000** |

Cash trace: $100{,}000 \xrightarrow{\times 3} 300{,}000 \xrightarrow{\times 1.7} 510{,}000$.

### The continuum of optimal strategies

The LP has a whole face of optima. Let $a\in[0,100{,}000]$:

$$x_1[1]=a,\quad x_2[1]=100{,}000-a,\quad x_2[2]=1.7a,\quad x_1[3]=3(100{,}000-a),\quad x_1[2]=s[2]=s[3]=s[4]=0$$

For every $a$ this yields $W = 5.1(100{,}000-a)+5.1a = 510{,}000$. Two extreme points:

| $a$ | Plan | Final wealth |
|---|---|---|
| $a=0$ | All 100,000 → Option 2 in Yr 1; 300,000 → Option 1 in Yr 3 | 510,000 |
| $a=100{,}000$ | All 100,000 → Option 1 in Yr 1; 170,000 → Option 2 in Yr 2 | 510,000 |

## 7. Optimality Certificate

**(a) Dominance argument.** Value per yuan available with $k$ years remaining, $g(k)$: $g(1)=1.7$; $g(2)=\max\{1.7^2,\,3\}=3$; $g(3)=\max\{1.7^3,\,1.7\cdot3,\,3\cdot1.7\}=5.1$. Since $5.1 > 4.913 = 1.7^3$ and $5.1 > 3$, no strategy can beat $5.1$ per yuan, so $W\le 100{,}000\times5.1=510{,}000$ — attained above.

**(b) LP dual.** With multipliers $\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_3$ on (C1)–(C3):

$$\min\; 100{,}000\,\pi_1 \quad \text{s.t. } \begin{aligned}
\pi_1 - 1.7\pi_2 &\ge 0 & (x_1[1])\\
\pi_1 - 3\pi_3 &\ge 0 & (x_2[1])\\
\pi_1 - \pi_2 &\ge 0 & (s[2])\\
\pi_2 - 1.7\pi_3 &\ge 0 & (x_1[2])\\
\pi_2 &\ge 3 & (x_2[2])\\
\pi_2 - \pi_3 &\ge 0 & (s[3])\\
\pi_3 &\ge 1.7 & (x_1[3])\\
\pi_3 &\ge 1 & (s[4])
\end{aligned}$$

The feasible dual point $\pi^*=(5.1,\;3,\;1.7)$ has objective $100{,}000\times5.1=510{,}000$, which equals the primal value — by strong duality the plan is optimal. *Economic reading of the duals:* one extra yuan at the beginning of Year 3 is worth 1.7 yuan at the end (use Option 1); at the beginning of Year 2 it is worth 3 yuan (use Option 2); at the beginning of Year 1 it is worth 5.1 yuan (use both options). Complementary slackness confirms $s[2]=s[3]=s[4]=x_1[2]=0$ at any optimum and leaves the free face parameterized by $a$ above.

## 8. Recommendation

**Invest the entire 100,000 yuan in the 2‑year option at the beginning of Year 1.** It matures at the end of Year 2 for 300,000 yuan; invest that entire 300,000 in the 1‑year option at the beginning of Year 3, which matures at the end of Year 3 for **510,000 yuan** (profit 410,000 yuan ≈ 4.1× the initial capital, ≈ 72.6 % p.a. compounded). The order may be reversed (1‑year first, then 2‑year) with identical results — the key is to fill the 3‑year horizon with exactly one 1‑year leg and one 2‑year leg, since $1.7\times3=5.1$ beats any other feasible combination.

# Multi-Period Investment Planning MILP

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $t \in T = \{0,1,2,3\}$ | Time periods (years) |
| $t \in T_A = \{0,1,2\}$ | Periods in which a product-A deposit may be started |
| $t \in T_B = \{0,1\}$ | Periods in which a product-B deposit may be started |
| $d \in D = \{2,4\}$ | Allowed durations (years) of a product-B program |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $W_0$ | 100,000 | Initial cash at $t=0$ (CNY) |
| $r_A$ | 1.7 | Return factor of product A (1 yuan → 1.7 yuan at $t+1$) |
| $r_B$ | 3.0 | Return factor of product B (1 yuan → 3 yuan at maturity) |
| $M$ | 100,000 | Big-M (≥ any feasible single investment) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (non-negative):**
- $a_t \ge 0,\ t\in T_A$ — yuan placed in product A at the beginning of year $t$ (returned $1.7\,a_t$ at $t+1$).
- $b_t \ge 0,\ t\in T_B$ — yuan placed in product B at the beginning of year $t$.
- $c_t \ge 0,\ t\in T$ — yuan held idle at the end of year $t$ (earns 0).

**Binary:**
- $z_{t,d}\in\{0,1\},\ t\in T_B,\ d\in D$ — equals 1 iff the B-program started at $t$ is held for $d$ years.

## 4. Model

$$
\boxed{\;\max\; W_3 \;=\; 1.7\,a_2 \;+\; 3\,b_1\,z_{1,2} \;+\; c_3\;}
$$

subject to

**Mutual exclusivity of B-durations (at most one duration per start date):**
$$
z_{t,2}+z_{t,4}\;\le\;1,\qquad t\in T_B=\{0,1\}
$$

**Big-M linking of chosen duration to invested amount:**
$$
b_t\;\le\;M\,(z_{t,2}+z_{t,4}),\qquad t\in T_B
$$
(so $b_t=0$ unless some duration is selected; if $z_{t,4}=1$ the funds are locked past $t=3$ and contribute nothing to the objective, so the optimizer will never use them.)

**Cash-flow balance at $t=0$:**
$$
a_0 + b_0 + c_0 \;=\; 100{,}000
$$

**Cash-flow balance at $t=1$** (only A-deposits started at $t=0$ mature; B started at $t=0$ is still locked):
$$
a_1 + b_1 + c_1 \;=\; 1.7\,a_0
$$

**Cash-flow balance at $t=2$** (A started at $t=1$ matures; B started at $t=0$ with $d=2$ matures; B started at $t=1$ is still locked until $t=3$):
$$
a_2 + c_2 \;=\; 1.7\,a_1 \;+\; 3\,b_0\,z_{0,2}
$$

**Terminal wealth identity at $t=3$** (A started at $t=2$ matures; B started at $t=1$ with $d=2$ matures):
$$
W_3 \;=\; 1.7\,a_2 \;+\; 3\,b_1\,z_{1,2} \;+\; c_3
$$

**Variable domains:**
$$
a_t\ge 0\ (t\in T_A),\quad b_t\ge 0\ (t\in T_B),\quad c_t\ge 0\ (t\in T),\quad z_{t,d}\in\{0,1\}\ (t\in T_B,d\in D)
$$

## 5. Explanation of the Model

* **Objective.** All wealth at $t=3$ comes from three sources: (i) A-deposits started at $t=2$ returning $1.7\,a_2$, (ii) B-deposits started at $t=1$ with the 2-year duration returning $3\,b_1\,z_{1,2}$, and (iii) any cash deliberately left idle $c_3$. Idle cash earns nothing, so the optimizer will minimize it whenever a positive-return alternative exists.

* **Mutual exclusivity + Big-M.** A B-deposit must be held for an integer multiple of 2 years. The binary $z_{t,d}$ selects which duration $d\in\{2,4\}$ is used at start date $t$. The big-M constraint $b_t\le M(z_{t,2}+z_{t,4})$ forces $b_t=0$ when no duration is chosen, and lets $b_t$ take any feasible value when one is. The duration $d=4$ matures after the horizon ($t+4>3$) and yields nothing, so the optimizer will set $z_{t,4}=0$ and $b_t=0$ in any optimal solution.

* **Cash-flow balances.** At every $t<3$, all cash received from maturing positions must be either reinvested (in $a_t$ or $b_t$) or held idle ($c_t$). At $t=2$ no new B can be started because $t+2=4>3$; only A is available. At $t=3$ no further investment is possible, so wealth equals the sum of maturities plus idle cash.

* **Alternative integer formulation.** Instead of the binaries $z_{t,d}$, one may introduce $k_t\in\{1,2\}$ (number of 2-year blocks) and replace the two constraints above with
$$
b_t \le M\,(2-k_t),\qquad k_t\in\{1,2\},\ t\in T_B,
$$
which is algebraically equivalent (since $k_t=1\Leftrightarrow d=2$ and $k_t=2\Leftrightarrow d=4$).

## 6. Sanity Check — Optimal Solution

The annualized return of A is $1.7-1=70\%$, while B held 2 years gives $\sqrt{3}-1\approx 73.2\%$ per year. Hence B dominates A whenever it can be held to maturity within the horizon.

* **Strategy 1:** Put 100,000 in B at $t=0$ → 300,000 at $t=2$ → put it all in A at $t=2$ → **510,000** at $t=3$.
* **Strategy 2:** Put 100,000 in A at $t=0$ → 170,000 at $t=1$ → put it all in B at $t=1$ → **510,000** at $t=3$.

Both yield 510,000 CNY, which is the optimum. The model will return either of these (or any convex combination) with objective value $W_3^\star = 510{,}000$.

**Continuous (non-negative):**

$$a_0 + b_0 + s_0 = W_0$$

$$a_1 + b_1 + s_1 = r_A\, a_0 + s_0$$

**(C3) Cash-flow balance at $t=2$** (no new B allowed; B started at $t=0$ with $d=2$ matures here):
$$a_2 + s_2 = r_A\, a_1 + r_B\, w_{0,2} + s_1$$

**(C4) Mutual exclusivity of B duration** at each start date:
$$z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} \leq 1, \quad t \in T_B$$

**(C5) Big-M linking** — can only invest in B if a duration is selected:
$$b_t \leq M\,(z_{t,2} + z_{t,4}), \quad t \in T_B$$

**(C6) Linearization of $w_{t,2} = b_t \cdot z_{t,2}$** (returns only occur if $d=2$ is chosen):
$$
\begin{aligned}
w_{t,2} &\leq b_t, \\
w_{t,2} &\leq M\, z_{t,2}, \\
w_{t,2} &\geq b_t - M\,(1 - z_{t,2}), \quad t \in T_B
\end{aligned}
$$

**(C7) Variable domains:**
$$
a_t \geq 0,\; b_t \geq 0,\; s_t \geq 0,\; w_{t,2} \geq 0,\quad z_{t,d} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Explanation of the Model

- **Product A** is modeled by $a_t$ for $t=0,1,2$. Each yuan invested at $t$ returns $1.7$ yuan at $t+1$, captured by $r_A a_t$ on the right-hand side of the next cash balance.

- **Terminal wealth** at $t=3$ consists of the maturing A-position $a_2$, the maturing B-position $w_{1,2}$ (from B started at $t=1$ with $d=2$), and residual idle cash $s_2$.

1. Continuous (fractional) investments allowed.
2. No transaction costs, taxes, or minimum investment thresholds.
3. All cash flows occur at integer year boundaries.
4. Reinvestment of all proceeds is permitted at any later date.
5. Idle cash earns zero interest.
6. $M = 500{,}000$ safely exceeds the maximum feasible cash in the system ($100{,}000 \times 1.7^3 \approx 491{,}513$).

# Multi-Period Investment Planning MILP

## 1. Problem Summary

An investor starts with **CNY 100,000** at $t=0$ and wishes to **maximize cash on hand at $t=3$**. Two products are available:

| Product | Type | Return factor | Possible start times |
|---------|------|---------------|----------------------|
| **A** | 1-year deposit | $1 \to 1.7$ | $t=0,1,2$ (matures $t+1$) |
| **B** | 2-year deposit | $1 \to 3$ | $t=0,1$ (matures $t+2$ or $t+4$) |

Idle cash earns 0 and is carried forward.

---

## 2. Sets, Parameters, Variables

### Sets
- $T=\{0,1,2,3\}$ — time periods
- $T_A=\{0,1,2\}$ — start times for product A
- $T_B=\{0,1\}$ — start times for product B
- $D=\{2,4\}$ — admissible durations for B (integer multiples of 2)

### Parameters
- $W_0 = 100{,}000$ — initial wealth
- $r_A = 1.7$ — return factor of A
- $r_B = 3$ — return factor of B
- $M = 10^{6}$ — big-M (any value $\geq W_0$ works)

### Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| $a_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Amount invested in product A starting at $t$ |
| $b_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Total amount invested in product B starting at $t$ |
| $u_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Amount of $b_t$ that matures **within** the horizon (linearization of $b_t z_{t,2}$) |
| $z_{t,d}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ iff the B-program started at $t$ has duration $d$ |
| $s_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Idle cash held at the end of period $t$ (carries to $t+1$) |

---

## 3. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{\;\max\; W_3 \;=\; r_A\,a_2 \;+\; r_B\,u_1 \;+\; s_2\;}
$$

This is exactly the cash in hand at $t=3$: A-investments started at $t=2$, B-investments started at $t=1$ with duration 2, plus any leftover idle cash from $t=2$.

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Cash-flow balance at each time

**(C0) Initial budget at $t=0$:**
$$
a_0 + b_0 + s_0 \;=\; W_0
$$

**(C1) Cash balance at $t=1$** (inflow = $1.7\,a_0$ from A-maturing plus idle carried from $t=0$):
$$
a_1 + b_1 + s_1 \;=\; r_A\,a_0 + s_0
$$

**(C2) Cash balance at $t=2$** (inflow = $1.7\,a_1$ from A plus $3\,u_0$ from B started at $t=0$ with duration 2, plus idle):
$$
a_2 + s_2 \;=\; r_A\,a_1 + r_B\,u_0 + s_1
$$

> Note: at $t=2$ no new B can be started (would mature at $t\ge 4$, beyond horizon). At $t=3$ no new investment is started (end of horizon).

### 4.2 Duration choice for B (mutual exclusivity)

**(C3) Exactly one duration per B-program:**
$$
z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

### 4.3 Big-M linking of duration to invested amount

These constraints linearize the product $b_t\,z_{t,2}$, ensuring that **only the portion of $b_t$ associated with duration 2 generates cash within the horizon**:

**(C4a)** $u_t$ cannot exceed the chosen duration-2 capacity:
$$
u_t \;\le\; M\,z_{t,2}, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

**(C4b)** $u_t$ cannot exceed the total B investment:
$$
u_t \;\le\; b_t, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

**(C4c)** If duration 2 is **not** chosen, $u_t$ must be 0:
$$
u_t \;\ge\; b_t - M\,(1-z_{t,2}), \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

> Equivalently, since $1-z_{t,2}=z_{t,4}$: $\;u_t \ge b_t - M\,z_{t,4}$.
> Logic:
> - If $z_{t,2}=1$: (C4a) is non-binding, (C4c) gives $u_t \ge b_t$, combined with (C4b) ⇒ $u_t = b_t$ (all matures at $t+2$).
> - If $z_{t,2}=0$: (C4c) gives $u_t \ge b_t - M$, (C4a) gives $u_t \le 0$, so $u_t = 0$ (nothing matures within horizon).

---

## 5. Complete MILP Summary

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max\;\; & 1.7\,a_2 + 3\,u_1 + s_2 \\[4pt]
\text{s.t.}\;\; & a_0 + b_0 + s_0 = 100{,}000 \\
& a_1 + b_1 + s_1 = 1.7\,a_0 + s_0 \\
& a_2 + s_2 = 1.7\,a_1 + 3\,u_0 + s_1 \\
& z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} = 1, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \le M\,z_{t,2}, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \le b_t, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \ge b_t - M\,(1-z_{t,2}), \quad t=0,1 \\
& a_t, b_t, u_t, s_t \ge 0 \\
& z_{t,d} \in \{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

| Element | Role |
|---------|------|
| $a_t$ | Captures the rolling 1-year deposit; $1.7\,a_t$ reappears at $t+1$. |
| $b_t$ | Total capital committed to B at $t$, regardless of duration. |
| $u_t$ | Linearization of $b_t z_{t,2}$: the share of B-capital that matures within the planning horizon. |
| $z_{t,2}, z_{t,4}$ | Choose whether the B-program started at $t$ matures at $t+2$ (in-horizon) or $t+4$ (out-of-horizon, yields nothing). |
| $s_t$ | Tracks idle cash so the model never forces illiquidity. |
| (C0)–(C2) | Conservation of cash: every yuan received is either reinvested or held idle. |
| (C3) | Enforces that each B-program has exactly one duration. |
| (C4a–c) | Big-M coupling: if duration 4 is chosen, no in-horizon cash flow arises from $b_t$. |

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Deterministic returns** — $1.7$ for A and $3$ for B are realized with certainty.
2. **No frictions** — no transaction costs, taxes, or minimum-investment constraints.
3. **No borrowing or short-selling.**
4. **Idle cash earns 0** and is fully carried to the next period.
5. **All cash must be allocated** at each period (to A, B, or idle).
6. **No new B at $t=2$** (would mature beyond $t=3$); **no new investment at $t=3$** (terminal period).
7. **Big-M valid**: $M=10^6 \ge W_0$ ensures constraints (C4) are non-restrictive when the corresponding binary is 1.

---

## 8. Optimal Solution (for verification)

Because $r_B=3$ over 2 years is equivalent to $1.7$ over 1 year followed by $3$ over 1 year (compounding factor $5.1$ either way), the optimal wealth is:

$$
W_3^{*} \;=\; 5.1 \times 100{,}000 \;=\; \mathbf{510{,}000\;CNY}
$$

Achieved, for example, by:
- $t=0$: $a_0=100{,}000,\ b_0=0,\ s_0=0$
- $t=1$: $a_1=0,\ b_1=170{,}000,\ s_1=0,\ z_{1,2}=1$
- $t=2$: $a_2=0,\ s_2=0$
- $t=3$: receive $3\times 170{,}000 = 510{,}000$.

(Equivalently: invest all in B at $t=0$ with duration 2, then reinvest the $300{,}000$ received at $t=2$ in A.)

response.content:
# Multi-Period Investment Planning MILP

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $t \in T = \{0,1,2,3\}$ | Time periods (years) |
| $t \in T_A = \{0,1,2\}$ | Periods in which a product-A deposit may be started |
| $t \in T_B = \{0,1\}$ | Periods in which a product-B deposit may be started |
| $d \in D = \{2,4\}$ | Allowed durations (years) of a product-B program |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $W_0$ | 100,000 | Initial cash at $t=0$ (CNY) |
| $r_A$ | 1.7 | Return factor of product A (1 yuan → 1.7 yuan at $t+1$) |
| $r_B$ | 3.0 | Return factor of product B (1 yuan → 3 yuan at maturity) |
| $M$ | 100,000 | Big-M (≥ any feasible single investment) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (non-negative):**
- $a_t \ge 0,\ t\in T_A$ — yuan placed in product A at the beginning of year $t$ (returned $1.7\,a_t$ at $t+1$).
- $b_t \ge 0,\ t\in T_B$ — yuan placed in product B at the beginning of year $t$.
- $c_t \ge 0,\ t\in T$ — yuan held idle at the end of year $t$ (earns 0).

**Binary:**
- $z_{t,d}\in\{0,1\},\ t\in T_B,\ d\in D$ — equals 1 iff the B-program started at $t$ is held for $d$ years.

## 4. Model

$$
\boxed{\;\max\; W_3 \;=\; 1.7\,a_2 \;+\; 3\,b_1\,z_{1,2} \;+\; c_3\;}
$$

subject to

**Mutual exclusivity of B-durations (at most one duration per start date):**
$$
z_{t,2}+z_{t,4}\;\le\;1,\qquad t\in T_B=\{0,1\}
$$

**Big-M linking of chosen duration to invested amount:**
$$
b_t\;\le\;M\,(z_{t,2}+z_{t,4}),\qquad t\in T_B
$$
(so $b_t=0$ unless some duration is selected; if $z_{t,4}=1$ the funds are locked past $t=3$ and contribute nothing to the objective, so the optimizer will never use them.)

**Cash-flow balance at $t=0$:**
$$
a_0 + b_0 + c_0 \;=\; 100{,}000
$$

**Cash-flow balance at $t=1$** (only A-deposits started at $t=0$ mature; B started at $t=0$ is still locked):
$$
a_1 + b_1 + c_1 \;=\; 1.7\,a_0
$$

**Cash-flow balance at $t=2$** (A started at $t=1$ matures; B started at $t=0$ with $d=2$ matures; B started at $t=1$ is still locked until $t=3$):
$$
a_2 + c_2 \;=\; 1.7\,a_1 \;+\; 3\,b_0\,z_{0,2}
$$

**Terminal wealth identity at $t=3$** (A started at $t=2$ matures; B started at $t=1$ with $d=2$ matures):
$$
W_3 \;=\; 1.7\,a_2 \;+\; 3\,b_1\,z_{1,2} \;+\; c_3
$$

**Variable domains:**
$$
a_t\ge 0\ (t\in T_A),\quad b_t\ge 0\ (t\in T_B),\quad c_t\ge 0\ (t\in T),\quad z_{t,d}\in\{0,1\}\ (t\in T_B,d\in D)
$$

## 5. Explanation of the Model

* **Objective.** All wealth at $t=3$ comes from three sources: (i) A-deposits started at $t=2$ returning $1.7\,a_2$, (ii) B-deposits started at $t=1$ with the 2-year duration returning $3\,b_1\,z_{1,2}$, and (iii) any cash deliberately left idle $c_3$. Idle cash earns nothing, so the optimizer will minimize it whenever a positive-return alternative exists.

* **Mutual exclusivity + Big-M.** A B-deposit must be held for an integer multiple of 2 years. The binary $z_{t,d}$ selects which duration $d\in\{2,4\}$ is used at start date $t$. The big-M constraint $b_t\le M(z_{t,2}+z_{t,4})$ forces $b_t=0$ when no duration is chosen, and lets $b_t$ take any feasible value when one is. The duration $d=4$ matures after the horizon ($t+4>3$) and yields nothing, so the optimizer will set $z_{t,4}=0$ and $b_t=0$ in any optimal solution.

* **Cash-flow balances.** At every $t<3$, all cash received from maturing positions must be either reinvested (in $a_t$ or $b_t$) or held idle ($c_t$). At $t=2$ no new B can be started because $t+2=4>3$; only A is available. At $t=3$ no further investment is possible, so wealth equals the sum of maturities plus idle cash.

* **Alternative integer formulation.** Instead of the binaries $z_{t,d}$, one may introduce $k_t\in\{1,2\}$ (number of 2-year blocks) and replace the two constraints above with
$$
b_t \le M\,(2-k_t),\qquad k_t\in\{1,2\},\ t\in T_B,
$$
which is algebraically equivalent (since $k_t=1\Leftrightarrow d=2$ and $k_t=2\Leftrightarrow d=4$).

## 6. Sanity Check — Optimal Solution

The annualized return of A is $1.7-1=70\%$, while B held 2 years gives $\sqrt{3}-1\approx 73.2\%$ per year. Hence B dominates A whenever it can be held to maturity within the horizon.

* **Strategy 1:** Put 100,000 in B at $t=0$ → 300,000 at $t=2$ → put it all in A at $t=2$ → **510,000** at $t=3$.
* **Strategy 2:** Put 100,000 in A at $t=0$ → 170,000 at $t=1$ → put it all in B at $t=1$ → **510,000** at $t=3$.

Both yield 510,000 CNY, which is the optimum. The model will return either of these (or any convex combination) with objective value $W_3^\star = 510{,}000$.

response.content:
# Multi-Period Investment Planning MILP

## 1. Sets and Indices
- $T = \{0,1,2,3\}$ — time periods (years)
- $T_A = \{0,1,2\}$ — admissible start dates for product A
- $T_B = \{0,1\}$ — admissible start dates for product B
- $D = \{2,4\}$ — admissible durations (in years) for product B

## 2. Parameters
| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|--------|-------|---------|
| $W_0$ | 100,000 | Initial cash at $t=0$ |
| $r_A$ | 1.7 | Return multiple of product A (1 + 0.7 profit) |
| $r_B$ | 3.0 | Return multiple of product B (1 + 2 profit) |
| $M$ | 500,000 | Big-M constant (≥ max feasible cash) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (non-negative):**
- $a_t \geq 0$, $t \in T_A$ — yuan placed in product A at start of year $t$ (matures at $t+1$)
- $b_t \geq 0$, $t \in T_B$ — yuan placed in product B at start of year $t$
- $s_t \geq 0$, $t \in \{0,1,2\}$ — idle cash held at the end of year $t$
- $w_{t,2} \geq 0$, $t \in T_B$ — auxiliary: portion of $b_t$ that matures at $t+2$ (i.e. $w_{t,2} = b_t \cdot z_{t,2}$)

**Binary:**
- $z_{t,d} \in \{0,1\}$, $t \in T_B$, $d \in D$ — 1 if duration $d$ is chosen for the B-program started at $t$

## 4. Objective Function
Maximize terminal wealth at $t=3$:
$$
\max \; Z \;=\; r_A\, a_2 \;+\; r_B\, w_{1,2} \;+\; s_2
$$
Interpretation: $1.7\times$ yuan of A maturing at $t=3$, $3\times$ yuan of B maturing at $t=3$, plus any idle cash.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Cash-flow balance at $t=0$:**
$$a_0 + b_0 + s_0 = W_0$$

**(C2) Cash-flow balance at $t=1$:**
$$a_1 + b_1 + s_1 = r_A\, a_0 + s_0$$

**(C3) Cash-flow balance at $t=2$** (no new B allowed; B started at $t=0$ with $d=2$ matures here):
$$a_2 + s_2 = r_A\, a_1 + r_B\, w_{0,2} + s_1$$

**(C4) Mutual exclusivity of B duration** at each start date:
$$z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} \leq 1, \quad t \in T_B$$

**(C5) Big-M linking** — can only invest in B if a duration is selected:
$$b_t \leq M\,(z_{t,2} + z_{t,4}), \quad t \in T_B$$

**(C6) Linearization of $w_{t,2} = b_t \cdot z_{t,2}$** (returns only occur if $d=2$ is chosen):
$$
\begin{aligned}
w_{t,2} &\leq b_t, \\
w_{t,2} &\leq M\, z_{t,2}, \\
w_{t,2} &\geq b_t - M\,(1 - z_{t,2}), \quad t \in T_B
\end{aligned}
$$

**(C7) Variable domains:**
$$
a_t \geq 0,\; b_t \geq 0,\; s_t \geq 0,\; w_{t,2} \geq 0,\quad z_{t,d} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Explanation of the Model

- **Product A** is modeled by $a_t$ for $t=0,1,2$. Each yuan invested at $t$ returns $1.7$ yuan at $t+1$, captured by $r_A a_t$ on the right-hand side of the next cash balance.
- **Product B** is modeled by $b_t$ for $t=0,1$. The binary $z_{t,d}$ selects the holding period:
  - $z_{t,2}=1$: matures at $t+2$ (within horizon), contributing $r_B w_{t,2}$ to cash at $t+2$.
  - $z_{t,4}=1$: matures at $t+4$ (after horizon), contributing nothing to cash at $t=3$ — modeled by $w_{t,2}=0$ via (C6).
- **Idle cash** $s_t$ absorbs any uninvested yuan and earns 0, satisfying "all cash received must be re-invested or held" through the equalities (C1)–(C3).
- **Big-M coupling** (C5)–(C6) ensures that if no short duration is chosen, no return is credited, while still allowing the optimizer to "lock up" funds in long-duration B if desired (a feasible but dominated choice).
- **Terminal wealth** at $t=3$ consists of the maturing A-position $a_2$, the maturing B-position $w_{1,2}$ (from B started at $t=1$ with $d=2$), and residual idle cash $s_2$.

## 7. Assumptions
1. Continuous (fractional) investments allowed.
2. No transaction costs, taxes, or minimum investment thresholds.
3. All cash flows occur at integer year boundaries.
4. Reinvestment of all proceeds is permitted at any later date.
5. Idle cash earns zero interest.
6. $M = 500{,}000$ safely exceeds the maximum feasible cash in the system ($100{,}000 \times 1.7^3 \approx 491{,}513$).

<benchmark text>

response.content:
# Multi-Period Investment Planning MILP

## 1. Problem Summary

An investor starts with **CNY 100,000** at $t=0$ and wishes to **maximize cash on hand at $t=3$**. Two products are available:

| Product | Type | Return factor | Possible start times |
|---------|------|---------------|----------------------|
| **A** | 1-year deposit | $1 \to 1.7$ | $t=0,1,2$ (matures $t+1$) |
| **B** | 2-year deposit | $1 \to 3$ | $t=0,1$ (matures $t+2$ or $t+4$) |

Idle cash earns 0 and is carried forward.

---

## 2. Sets, Parameters, Variables

### Sets
- $T=\{0,1,2,3\}$ — time periods
- $T_A=\{0,1,2\}$ — start times for product A
- $T_B=\{0,1\}$ — start times for product B
- $D=\{2,4\}$ — admissible durations for B (integer multiples of 2)

### Parameters
- $W_0 = 100{,}000$ — initial wealth
- $r_A = 1.7$ — return factor of A
- $r_B = 3$ — return factor of B
- $M = 10^{6}$ — big-M (any value $\geq W_0$ works)

### Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| $a_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Amount invested in product A starting at $t$ |
| $b_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Total amount invested in product B starting at $t$ |
| $u_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Amount of $b_t$ that matures **within** the horizon (linearization of $b_t z_{t,2}$) |
| $z_{t,d}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ iff the B-program started at $t$ has duration $d$ |
| $s_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Idle cash held at the end of period $t$ (carries to $t+1$) |

---

## 3. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{\;\max\; W_3 \;=\; r_A\,a_2 \;+\; r_B\,u_1 \;+\; s_2\;}
$$

This is exactly the cash in hand at $t=3$: A-investments started at $t=2$, B-investments started at $t=1$ with duration 2, plus any leftover idle cash from $t=2$.

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Cash-flow balance at each time

**(C0) Initial budget at $t=0$:**
$$
a_0 + b_0 + s_0 \;=\; W_0
$$

**(C1) Cash balance at $t=1$** (inflow = $1.7\,a_0$ from A-maturing plus idle carried from $t=0$):
$$
a_1 + b_1 + s_1 \;=\; r_A\,a_0 + s_0
$$

**(C2) Cash balance at $t=2$** (inflow = $1.7\,a_1$ from A plus $3\,u_0$ from B started at $t=0$ with duration 2, plus idle):
$$
a_2 + s_2 \;=\; r_A\,a_1 + r_B\,u_0 + s_1
$$

> Note: at $t=2$ no new B can be started (would mature at $t\ge 4$, beyond horizon). At $t=3$ no new investment is started (end of horizon).

### 4.2 Duration choice for B (mutual exclusivity)

**(C3) Exactly one duration per B-program:**
$$
z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

### 4.3 Big-M linking of duration to invested amount

These constraints linearize the product $b_t\,z_{t,2}$, ensuring that **only the portion of $b_t$ associated with duration 2 generates cash within the horizon**:

**(C4a)** $u_t$ cannot exceed the chosen duration-2 capacity:
$$
u_t \;\le\; M\,z_{t,2}, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

**(C4b)** $u_t$ cannot exceed the total B investment:
$$
u_t \;\le\; b_t, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

**(C4c)** If duration 2 is **not** chosen, $u_t$ must be 0:
$$
u_t \;\ge\; b_t - M\,(1-z_{t,2}), \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

> Equivalently, since $1-z_{t,2}=z_{t,4}$: $\;u_t \ge b_t - M\,z_{t,4}$.
> Logic:
> - If $z_{t,2}=1$: (C4a) is non-binding, (C4c) gives $u_t \ge b_t$, combined with (C4b) ⇒ $u_t = b_t$ (all matures at $t+2$).
> - If $z_{t,2}=0$: (C4c) gives $u_t \ge b_t - M$, (C4a) gives $u_t \le 0$, so $u_t = 0$ (nothing matures within horizon).

---

## 5. Complete MILP Summary

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max\;\; & 1.7\,a_2 + 3\,u_1 + s_2 \\[4pt]
\text{s.t.}\;\; & a_0 + b_0 + s_0 = 100{,}000 \\
& a_1 + b_1 + s_1 = 1.7\,a_0 + s_0 \\
& a_2 + s_2 = 1.7\,a_1 + 3\,u_0 + s_1 \\
& z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} = 1, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \le M\,z_{t,2}, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \le b_t, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \ge b_t - M\,(1-z_{t,2}), \quad t=0,1 \\
& a_t, b_t, u_t, s_t \ge 0 \\
& z_{t,d} \in \{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

| Element | Role |
|---------|------|
| $a_t$ | Captures the rolling 1-year deposit; $1.7\,a_t$ reappears at $t+1$. |
| $b_t$ | Total capital committed to B at $t$, regardless of duration. |
| $u_t$ | Linearization of $b_t z_{t,2}$: the share of B-capital that matures within the planning horizon. |
| $z_{t,2}, z_{t,4}$ | Choose whether the B-program started at $t$ matures at $t+2$ (in-horizon) or $t+4$ (out-of-horizon, yields nothing). |
| $s_t$ | Tracks idle cash so the model never forces illiquidity. |
| (C0)–(C2) | Conservation of cash: every yuan received is either reinvested or held idle. |
| (C3) | Enforces that each B-program has exactly one duration. |
| (C4a–c) | Big-M coupling: if duration 4 is chosen, no in-horizon cash flow arises from $b_t$. |

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Deterministic returns** — $1.7$ for A and $3$ for B are realized with certainty.
2. **No frictions** — no transaction costs, taxes, or minimum-investment constraints.
3. **No borrowing or short-selling.**
4. **Idle cash earns 0** and is fully carried to the next period.
5. **All cash must be allocated** at each period (to A, B, or idle).
6. **No new B at $t=2$** (would mature beyond $t=3$); **no new investment at $t=3$** (terminal period).
7. **Big-M valid**: $M=10^6 \ge W_0$ ensures constraints (C4) are non-restrictive when the corresponding binary is 1.

---

## 8. Optimal Solution (for verification)

Because $r_B=3$ over 2 years is equivalent to $1.7$ over 1 year followed by $3$ over 1 year (compounding factor $5.1$ either way), the optimal wealth is:

$$
W_3^{*} \;=\; 5.1 \times 100{,}000 \;=\; \mathbf{510{,}000\;CNY}
$$

Achieved, for example, by:
- $t=0$: $a_0=100{,}000,\ b_0=0,\ s_0=0$
- $t=1$: $a_1=0,\ b_1=170{,}000,\ s_1=0,\ z_{1,2}=1$
- $t=2$: $a_2=0,\ s_2=0$
- $t=3$: receive $3\times 170{,}000 = 510{,}000$.

(Equivalently: invest all in B at $t=0$ with duration 2, then reinvest the $300{,}000$ received at $t=2$ in A.)

Model 1:
# Multi-Period Investment Planning MILP

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $t \in T = \{0,1,2,3\}$ | Time periods (years) |
| $t \in T_A = \{0,1,2\}$ | Periods in which a product-A deposit may be started |
| $t \in T_B = \{0,1\}$ | Periods in which a product-B deposit may be started |
| $d \in D = \{2,4\}$ | Allowed durations (years) of a product-B program |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $W_0$ | 100,000 | Initial cash at $t=0$ (CNY) |
| $r_A$ | 1.7 | Return factor of product A (1 yuan → 1.7 yuan at $t+1$) |
| $r_B$ | 3.0 | Return factor of product B (1 yuan → 3 yuan at maturity) |
| $M$ | 100,000 | Big-M (≥ any feasible single investment) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (non-negative):**
- $a_t \ge 0,\ t\in T_A$ — yuan placed in product A at the beginning of year $t$ (returned $1.7\,a_t$ at $t+1$).
- $b_t \ge 0,\ t\in T_B$ — yuan placed in product B at the beginning of year $t$.
- $c_t \ge 0,\ t\in T$ — yuan held idle at the end of year $t$ (earns 0).

**Binary:**
- $z_{t,d}\in\{0,1\},\ t\in T_B,\ d\in D$ — equals 1 iff the B-program started at $t$ is held for $d$ years.

## 4. Model

$$
\boxed{\;\max\; W_3 \;=\; 1.7\,a_2 \;+\; 3\,b_1\,z_{1,2} \;+\; c_3\;}
$$

subject to

**Mutual exclusivity of B-durations (at most one duration per start date):**
$$
z_{t,2}+z_{t,4}\;\le\;1,\qquad t\in T_B=\{0,1\}
$$

**Big-M linking of chosen duration to invested amount:**
$$
b_t\;\le\;M\,(z_{t,2}+z_{t,4}),\qquad t\in T_B
$$
(so $b_t=0$ unless some duration is selected; if $z_{t,4}=1$ the funds are locked past $t=3$ and contribute nothing to the objective, so the optimizer will never use them.)

**Cash-flow balance at $t=0$:**
$$
a_0 + b_0 + c_0 \;=\; 100{,}000
$$

**Cash-flow balance at $t=1$** (only A-deposits started at $t=0$ mature; B started at $t=0$ is still locked):
$$
a_1 + b_1 + c_1 \;=\; 1.7\,a_0
$$

**Cash-flow balance at $t=2$** (A started at $t=1$ matures; B started at $t=0$ with $d=2$ matures; B started at $t=1$ is still locked until $t=3$):
$$
a_2 + c_2 \;=\; 1.7\,a_1 \;+\; 3\,b_0\,z_{0,2}
$$

**Terminal wealth identity at $t=3$** (A started at $t=2$ matures; B started at $t=1$ with $d=2$ matures):
$$
W_3 \;=\; 1.7\,a_2 \;+\; 3\,b_1\,z_{1,2} \;+\; c_3
$$

**Variable domains:**
$$
a_t\ge 0\ (t\in T_A),\quad b_t\ge 0\ (t\in T_B),\quad c_t\ge 0\ (t\in T),\quad z_{t,d}\in\{0,1\}\ (t\in T_B,d\in D)
$$

## 5. Explanation of the Model

* **Objective.** All wealth at $t=3$ comes from three sources: (i) A-deposits started at $t=2$ returning $1.7\,a_2$, (ii) B-deposits started at $t=1$ with the 2-year duration returning $3\,b_1\,z_{1,2}$, and (iii) any cash deliberately left idle $c_3$. Idle cash earns nothing, so the optimizer will minimize it whenever a positive-return alternative exists.

* **Mutual exclusivity + Big-M.** A B-deposit must be held for an integer multiple of 2 years. The binary $z_{t,d}$ selects which duration $d\in\{2,4\}$ is used at start date $t$. The big-M constraint $b_t\le M(z_{t,2}+z_{t,4})$ forces $b_t=0$ when no duration is chosen, and lets $b_t$ take any feasible value when one is. The duration $d=4$ matures after the horizon ($t+4>3$) and yields nothing, so the optimizer will set $z_{t,4}=0$ and $b_t=0$ in any optimal solution.

* **Cash-flow balances.** At every $t<3$, all cash received from maturing positions must be either reinvested (in $a_t$ or $b_t$) or held idle ($c_t$). At $t=2$ no new B can be started because $t+2=4>3$; only A is available. At $t=3$ no further investment is possible, so wealth equals the sum of maturities plus idle cash.

* **Alternative integer formulation.** Instead of the binaries $z_{t,d}$, one may introduce $k_t\in\{1,2\}$ (number of 2-year blocks) and replace the two constraints above with
$$
b_t \le M\,(2-k_t),\qquad k_t\in\{1,2\},\ t\in T_B,
$$
which is algebraically equivalent (since $k_t=1\Leftrightarrow d=2$ and $k_t=2\Leftrightarrow d=4$).

## 6. Sanity Check — Optimal Solution

The annualized return of A is $1.7-1=70\%$, while B held 2 years gives $\sqrt{3}-1\approx 73.2\%$ per year. Hence B dominates A whenever it can be held to maturity within the horizon.

* **Strategy 1:** Put 100,000 in B at $t=0$ → 300,000 at $t=2$ → put it all in A at $t=2$ → **510,000** at $t=3$.
* **Strategy 2:** Put 100,000 in A at $t=0$ → 170,000 at $t=1$ → put it all in B at $t=1$ → **510,000** at $t=3$.

Both yield 510,000 CNY, which is the optimum. The model will return either of these (or any convex combination) with objective value $W_3^\star = 510{,}000$.

# Multi-Period Investment Planning MILP

## 1. Sets and Indices
- $T = \{0,1,2,3\}$ — time periods (years)
- $T_A = \{0,1,2\}$ — admissible start dates for product A
- $T_B = \{0,1\}$ — admissible start dates for product B
- $D = \{2,4\}$ — admissible durations (in years) for product B

## 2. Parameters
| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|--------|-------|---------|
| $W_0$ | 100,000 | Initial cash at $t=0$ |
| $r_A$ | 1.7 | Return multiple of product A (1 + 0.7 profit) |
| $r_B$ | 3.0 | Return multiple of product B (1 + 2 profit) |
| $M$ | 500,000 | Big-M constant (≥ max feasible cash) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous (non-negative):**
- $a_t \geq 0$, $t \in T_A$ — yuan placed in product A at start of year $t$ (matures at $t+1$)
- $b_t \geq 0$, $t \in T_B$ — yuan placed in product B at start of year $t$
- $s_t \geq 0$, $t \in \{0,1,2\}$ — idle cash held at the end of year $t$
- $w_{t,2} \geq 0$, $t \in T_B$ — auxiliary: portion of $b_t$ that matures at $t+2$ (i.e. $w_{t,2} = b_t \cdot z_{t,2}$)

**Binary:**
- $z_{t,d} \in \{0,1\}$, $t \in T_B$, $d \in D$ — 1 if duration $d$ is chosen for the B-program started at $t$

## 4. Objective Function
Maximize terminal wealth at $t=3$:
$$
\max \; Z \;=\; r_A\, a_2 \;+\; r_B\, w_{1,2} \;+\; s_2
$$
Interpretation: $1.7\times$ yuan of A maturing at $t=3$, $3\times$ yuan of B maturing at $t=3$, plus any idle cash.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Cash-flow balance at $t=0$:**
$$a_0 + b_0 + s_0 = W_0$$

**(C2) Cash-flow balance at $t=1$:**
$$a_1 + b_1 + s_1 = r_A\, a_0 + s_0$$

**(C3) Cash-flow balance at $t=2$** (no new B allowed; B started at $t=0$ with $d=2$ matures here):
$$a_2 + s_2 = r_A\, a_1 + r_B\, w_{0,2} + s_1$$

**(C4) Mutual exclusivity of B duration** at each start date:
$$z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} \leq 1, \quad t \in T_B$$

**(C5) Big-M linking** — can only invest in B if a duration is selected:
$$b_t \leq M\,(z_{t,2} + z_{t,4}), \quad t \in T_B$$

**(C6) Linearization of $w_{t,2} = b_t \cdot z_{t,2}$** (returns only occur if $d=2$ is chosen):
$$
\begin{aligned}
w_{t,2} &\leq b_t, \\
w_{t,2} &\leq M\, z_{t,2}, \\
w_{t,2} &\geq b_t - M\,(1 - z_{t,2}), \quad t \in T_B
\end{aligned}
$$

**(C7) Variable domains:**
$$
a_t \geq 0,\; b_t \geq 0,\; s_t \geq 0,\; w_{t,2} \geq 0,\quad z_{t,d} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Explanation of the Model

- **Product A** is modeled by $a_t$ for $t=0,1,2$. Each yuan invested at $t$ returns $1.7$ yuan at $t+1$, captured by $r_A a_t$ on the right-hand side of the next cash balance.
- **Product B** is modeled by $b_t$ for $t=0,1$. The binary $z_{t,d}$ selects the holding period:
  - $z_{t,2}=1$: matures at $t+2$ (within horizon), contributing $r_B w_{t,2}$ to cash at $t+2$.
  - $z_{t,4}=1$: matures at $t+4$ (after horizon), contributing nothing to cash at $t=3$ — modeled by $w_{t,2}=0$ via (C6).
- **Idle cash** $s_t$ absorbs any uninvested yuan and earns 0, satisfying "all cash received must be re-invested or held" through the equalities (C1)–(C3).
- **Big-M coupling** (C5)–(C6) ensures that if no short duration is chosen, no return is credited, while still allowing the optimizer to "lock up" funds in long-duration B if desired (a feasible but dominated choice).
- **Terminal wealth** at $t=3$ consists of the maturing A-position $a_2$, the maturing B-position $w_{1,2}$ (from B started at $t=1$ with $d=2$), and residual idle cash $s_2$.

## 7. Assumptions
1. Continuous (fractional) investments allowed.
2. No transaction costs, taxes, or minimum investment thresholds.
3. All cash flows occur at integer year boundaries.
4. Reinvestment of all proceeds is permitted at any later date.
5. Idle cash earns zero interest.
6. $M = 500{,}000$ safely exceeds the maximum feasible cash in the system ($100{,}000 \times 1.7^3 \approx 491{,}513$).

Model 4:
# Multi-Period Investment Planning MILP

## 1. Problem Summary

An investor starts with **CNY 100,000** at $t=0$ and wishes to **maximize cash on hand at $t=3$**. Two products are available:

| Product | Type | Return factor | Possible start times |
|---------|------|---------------|----------------------|
| **A** | 1-year deposit | $1 \to 1.7$ | $t=0,1,2$ (matures $t+1$) |
| **B** | 2-year deposit | $1 \to 3$ | $t=0,1$ (matures $t+2$ or $t+4$) |

Idle cash earns 0 and is carried forward.

---

## 2. Sets, Parameters, Variables

### Sets
- $T=\{0,1,2,3\}$ — time periods
- $T_A=\{0,1,2\}$ — start times for product A
- $T_B=\{0,1\}$ — start times for product B
- $D=\{2,4\}$ — admissible durations for B (integer multiples of 2)

### Parameters
- $W_0 = 100{,}000$ — initial wealth
- $r_A = 1.7$ — return factor of A
- $r_B = 3$ — return factor of B
- $M = 10^{6}$ — big-M (any value $\geq W_0$ works)

### Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| $a_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Amount invested in product A starting at $t$ |
| $b_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Total amount invested in product B starting at $t$ |
| $u_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Amount of $b_t$ that matures **within** the horizon (linearization of $b_t z_{t,2}$) |
| $z_{t,d}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ iff the B-program started at $t$ has duration $d$ |
| $s_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Idle cash held at the end of period $t$ (carries to $t+1$) |

---

## 3. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{\;\max\; W_3 \;=\; r_A\,a_2 \;+\; r_B\,u_1 \;+\; s_2\;}
$$

This is exactly the cash in hand at $t=3$: A-investments started at $t=2$, B-investments started at $t=1$ with duration 2, plus any leftover idle cash from $t=2$.

---

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Cash-flow balance at each time

**(C0) Initial budget at $t=0$:**
$$
a_0 + b_0 + s_0 \;=\; W_0
$$

**(C1) Cash balance at $t=1$** (inflow = $1.7\,a_0$ from A-maturing plus idle carried from $t=0$):
$$
a_1 + b_1 + s_1 \;=\; r_A\,a_0 + s_0
$$

**(C2) Cash balance at $t=2$** (inflow = $1.7\,a_1$ from A plus $3\,u_0$ from B started at $t=0$ with duration 2, plus idle):
$$
a_2 + s_2 \;=\; r_A\,a_1 + r_B\,u_0 + s_1
$$

> Note: at $t=2$ no new B can be started (would mature at $t\ge 4$, beyond horizon). At $t=3$ no new investment is started (end of horizon).

### 4.2 Duration choice for B (mutual exclusivity)

**(C3) Exactly one duration per B-program:**
$$
z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

### 4.3 Big-M linking of duration to invested amount

These constraints linearize the product $b_t\,z_{t,2}$, ensuring that **only the portion of $b_t$ associated with duration 2 generates cash within the horizon**:

**(C4a)** $u_t$ cannot exceed the chosen duration-2 capacity:
$$
u_t \;\le\; M\,z_{t,2}, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

**(C4b)** $u_t$ cannot exceed the total B investment:
$$
u_t \;\le\; b_t, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

**(C4c)** If duration 2 is **not** chosen, $u_t$ must be 0:
$$
u_t \;\ge\; b_t - M\,(1-z_{t,2}), \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B
$$

> Equivalently, since $1-z_{t,2}=z_{t,4}$: $\;u_t \ge b_t - M\,z_{t,4}$.
> Logic:
> - If $z_{t,2}=1$: (C4a) is non-binding, (C4c) gives $u_t \ge b_t$, combined with (C4b) ⇒ $u_t = b_t$ (all matures at $t+2$).
> - If $z_{t,2}=0$: (C4c) gives $u_t \ge b_t - M$, (C4a) gives $u_t \le 0$, so $u_t = 0$ (nothing matures within horizon).

---

## 5. Complete MILP Summary

$$
\begin{aligned}
\max\;\; & 1.7\,a_2 + 3\,u_1 + s_2 \\[4pt]
\text{s.t.}\;\; & a_0 + b_0 + s_0 = 100{,}000 \\
& a_1 + b_1 + s_1 = 1.7\,a_0 + s_0 \\
& a_2 + s_2 = 1.7\,a_1 + 3\,u_0 + s_1 \\
& z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} = 1, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \le M\,z_{t,2}, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \le b_t, \quad t=0,1 \\
& u_t \ge b_t - M\,(1-z_{t,2}), \quad t=0,1 \\
& a_t, b_t, u_t, s_t \ge 0 \\
& z_{t,d} \in \{0,1\}
\end{aligned}
$$

---

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

| Element | Role |
|---------|------|
| $a_t$ | Captures the rolling 1-year deposit; $1.7\,a_t$ reappears at $t+1$. |
| $b_t$ | Total capital committed to B at $t$, regardless of duration. |
| $u_t$ | Linearization of $b_t z_{t,2}$: the share of B-capital that matures within the planning horizon. |
| $z_{t,2}, z_{t,4}$ | Choose whether the B-program started at $t$ matures at $t+2$ (in-horizon) or $t+4$ (out-of-horizon, yields nothing). |
| $s_t$ | Tracks idle cash so the model never forces illiquidity. |
| (C0)–(C2) | Conservation of cash: every yuan received is either reinvested or held idle. |
| (C3) | Enforces that each B-program has exactly one duration. |
| (C4a–c) | Big-M coupling: if duration 4 is chosen, no in-horizon cash flow arises from $b_t$. |

---

## 7. Assumptions

1. **Deterministic returns** — $1.7$ for A and $3$ for B are realized with certainty.
2. **No frictions** — no transaction costs, taxes, or minimum-investment constraints.
3. **No borrowing or short-selling.**
4. **Idle cash earns 0** and is fully carried to the next period.
5. **All cash must be allocated** at each period (to A, B, or idle).
6. **No new B at $t=2$** (would mature beyond $t=3$); **no new investment at $t=3$** (terminal period).
7. **Big-M valid**: $M=10^6 \ge W_0$ ensures constraints (C4) are non-restrictive when the corresponding binary is 1.

---

## 8. Optimal Solution (for verification)

Because $r_B=3$ over 2 years is equivalent to $1.7$ over 1 year followed by $3$ over 1 year (compounding factor $5.1$ either way), the optimal wealth is:

$$
W_3^{*} \;=\; 5.1 \times 100{,}000 \;=\; \mathbf{510{,}000\;CNY}
$$

Achieved, for example, by:
- $t=0$: $a_0=100{,}000,\ b_0=0,\ s_0=0$
- $t=1$: $a_1=0,\ b_1=170{,}000,\ s_1=0,\ z_{1,2}=1$
- $t=2$: $a_2=0,\ s_2=0$
- $t=3$: receive $3\times 170{,}000 = 510{,}000$.

(Equivalently: invest all in B at $t=0$ with duration 2, then reinvest the $300{,}000$ received at $t=2$ in A.)

## Best model selected (from the generated candidates)

Among the six candidates, the **time‑indexed cash‑flow model with a big‑M linearization of the product $b_t z_{t,2}$** is the strongest: it is complete (every cash flow traced, no free/unbounded variable), it handles the "multiple of two years" rule explicitly with binaries, and it yields the provably correct optimum. I present it below in full, with the reasoning and the optimal investment plan.

---

# Multi‑Period Investment Planning Model (MILP)

## 1. Problem statement and modeling assumptions

The investor holds $W_0 = 100{,}000$ CNY at $t=0$ and wants to **maximize the cash he owns at the end of year 3 ($t=3$)**.

| Product | Rule |
|---|---|
| **A** – 1‑year deposit | 1 yuan invested returns $1 + 0.7 = 1.7$ yuan one year later; it may be **rolled over** every year, and all proceeds may be reinvested later. |
| **B** – 2‑year deposit | 1 yuan invested returns $1 + 2 = 3$ yuan; it **must be held for an integer multiple of 2 years** ($k \cdot 2$ years, $k=1,2,\dots$). |

**Assumptions** (marked as *assumed* because the text leaves them open):
1. *(Assumed)* Returns are deterministic (guaranteed); 1 yuan in A → 1.7 yuan after 1 year; 1 yuan in B → 3 yuan after $2k$ years.
2. *(Assumed)* The 3‑year horizon is a set of annual decision epochs $t=0,1,2,3$; money can be invested only at the start of a year and matures at a year boundary.
3. *(Assumed)* Capital is divisible (continuous variables), no transaction costs, no taxes, no minimum ticket, no borrowing/short selling.
4. *(Assumed)* Idle (uninvested) cash earns 0 % and is carried forward to the next epoch.
5. *(Assumed)* **Only cash flows realized on or before $t=3$ count.** A B‑position that matures at $t=4$ (i.e. $k=2$) is locked past the horizon and therefore contributes nothing at $t=3$; such a choice is strictly dominated and will never be optimal.
6. *(Assumed)* Proceeds may be split arbitrarily between A, B and idle cash at each epoch (no indivisibility of the principal).

## 2. Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $T=\{0,1,2,3\}$ | — | Decision epochs (years) |
| $T_A=\{0,1,2\}$ | — | Start times at which product A can be bought (matures $t+1\le 3$) |
| $T_B=\{0,1\}$ | — | Start times at which product B can be bought (matures $t+2\le 3$) |
| $D=\{2,4\}$ | — | Admissible holding periods of B (integer multiples of 2 years) |
| $W_0$ | $100{,}000$ | Initial capital (CNY) |
| $\rho_A$ | $1.7$ | Return factor of A: 1 yuan $\to 1.7$ yuan at $t+1$ |
| $\rho_B$ | $3.0$ | Return factor of B: 1 yuan $\to 3$ yuan at maturity |
| $M$ | $500{,}000$ | Big‑M (≥ any feasible $b_t$; max reachable cash $=100{,}000\cdot1.7^3\approx491{,}513$) |

## 3. Decision variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$, $t\in T_A$ | Yuan placed in product **A** at the beginning of year $t$ (matures at $t+1$, returning $1.7\,a_t$) |
| $b_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$, $t\in T_B$ | Total yuan placed in product **B** at the beginning of year $t$ |
| $u_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$, $t\in T_B$ | Portion of $b_t$ whose B‑program matures at $t+2$, i.e. the linearization of $b_t z_{t,2}$ |
| $s_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$, $t\in\{0,1,2\}$ | Idle cash held at the end of year $t$ (0 % return), carried to $t+1$ |
| $z_{t,d}$ | $\{0,1\}$, $t\in T_B,\ d\in D$ | $=1$ iff the B‑program started at $t$ is held exactly $d$ years ($d\in\{2,4\}$) |

## 4. Objective function

$$
\boxed{\max \; W_3 \;=\; 1.7\,a_2 \;+\; 3\,u_1 \;+\; s_2}
$$

Cash at $t=3$ has exactly three sources: (i) the A‑deposit started at $t=2$ (matures $t=3$): $1.7a_2$; (ii) the B‑deposit started at $t=1$ held 2 years (matures $t=3$): $3u_1$; (iii) idle cash carried from $t=2$: $s_2$.

## 5. Constraints

**(C0) Initial budget, $t=0$**
$$a_0 + b_0 + s_0 \;=\; 100{,}000$$

**(C1) Cash balance, $t=1$** (only $a_0$ matures; B started at $t=0$ is locked)
$$a_1 + b_1 + s_1 \;=\; 1.7\,a_0 \;+\; s_0$$

**(C2) Cash balance, $t=2$** (A started at $t=1$ matures; B started at $t=0$ with $d=2$ matures; no new B can start at $t=2$ because $t+2=4>3$)
$$a_2 + s_2 \;=\; 1.7\,a_1 \;+\; 3\,u_0 \;+\; s_1$$

**(C3) One holding period per B‑program** (multiples of 2 years)
$$z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B$$

**(C4–C6) Linearization of $u_t = b_t z_{t,2}$** (only the 2‑year program generates cash inside the horizon)
$$
\begin{aligned}
u_t &\le M\,z_{t,2}, &&\forall t\in T_B\\
u_t &\le b_t, &&\forall t\in T_B\\
u_t &\ge b_t - M\,(1-z_{t,2}), &&\forall t\in T_B
\end{aligned}
$$

**(C7) Domains**
$$a_t,b_t,u_t,s_t \ge 0,\qquad z_{t,d}\in\{0,1\}$$

## 6. Why the model is correct

* **Cash conservation.** (C0)–(C2) say that at every epoch all money available is split among A, B and idle cash; nothing is created or lost. The objective equals the wealth liquid at $t=3$, so maximizing it maximizes "money earned by the end of the third year".
* **Multiple‑of‑2‑years rule.** The binaries $z_{t,d}$ with $d\in\{2,4\}$ (C3) force every B‑position to be held for an integer multiple of two years; (C4)–(C6) ensure a position only pays out inside the horizon if the 2‑year option was chosen ($z_{t,4}=1 \Rightarrow u_t=0$, i.e. the money is locked until $t=4$ and is worthless at $t=3$ — never optimal, hence harmless).
* **Rolling of A.** $a_t$ is defined at every epoch, so the 1‑year deposit can be renewed year after year ($1.7\to2.89\to4.913$).
* **No unbounded variable.** Every variable appears in at least one equality or in the objective with a bounded antecedent (contrast with the candidate that used an unbounded $s_3$).

## 7. Optimal solution (verification)

Annualized: A gives $1.7$ per year; B gives $\sqrt{3}\approx1.732$ per year, and over a 2‑year block $3 > 1.7^2 = 2.89$, so **B beats A whenever it can be held to maturity inside the horizon**, and the last (third) year can only use A.

*Plan P1:* $t=0$: all $100{,}000$ into **B** (2‑year) → $t=2$: $300{,}000$ received → $t=2$: all $300{,}000$ into **A** → $t=3$: $1.7\times300{,}000 = \mathbf{510{,}000}$.

*Plan P2:* $t=0$: all $100{,}000$ into **A** → $t=1$: $170{,}000$ received → $t=1$: all $170{,}000$ into **B** (2‑year) → $t=3$: $3\times170{,}000 = \mathbf{510{,}000}$.

**Optimal value:** $W_3^{\star} = 100{,}000\times3\times1.7 = 510{,}000$ CNY (profit $=410{,}000$ CNY).

Because every yuan of initial capital can be shown to earn at most $1.7\times3 = 5.1$ by $t=3$ (A→A→A gives $4.913$, B→A gives $5.1$, A→B gives $5.1$), the model attains the upper bound $510{,}000$ and the solution is optimal. The optimum is **degenerate**: any split $x\in[0,100{,}000]$ placed in A at $t=0$ (then B at $t=1$) and $100{,}000-x$ in B at $t=0$ (then A at $t=2$) gives the same $510{,}000$.

**Model‑class remark.** Because the horizon is only 3 years, the only admissible in‑horizon duration is $2$ years, so the MILP above reduces to a pure LP if one drops the binaries and simply forbids B‑start at $t=2$; the binaries are kept because they are what enforces the "multiple of two years" rule in general and are needed as soon as a longer horizon is considered.

## Best model selected (from the generated candidates)

Among the six candidates, the **time‑indexed cash‑flow model with a big‑M linearization of the product $b_t z_{t,2}$** is the strongest: it is complete (every cash flow traced, no free/unbounded variable), it handles the "multiple of two years" rule explicitly with binaries, and it yields the provably correct optimum. I present it below in full, with the reasoning and the optimal investment plan.

---

# Multi‑Period Investment Planning Model (MILP)

## 1. Problem statement and modeling assumptions

The investor holds $W_0 = 100{,}000$ CNY at $t=0$ and wants to **maximize the cash he owns at the end of year 3 ($t=3$)**.

| Product | Rule |
|---|---|
| **A** – 1‑year deposit | 1 yuan invested returns $1 + 0.7 = 1.7$ yuan one year later; it may be **rolled over** every year, and all proceeds may be reinvested later. |
| **B** – 2‑year deposit | 1 yuan invested returns $1 + 2 = 3$ yuan; it **must be held for an integer multiple of 2 years** ($k \cdot 2$ years, $k=1,2,\dots$). |

**Assumptions** (marked as *assumed* because the text leaves them open):
1. *(Assumed)* Returns are deterministic (guaranteed); 1 yuan in A → 1.7 yuan after 1 year; 1 yuan in B → 3 yuan after $2k$ years.
2. *(Assumed)* The 3‑year horizon is a set of annual decision epochs $t=0,1,2,3$; money can be invested only at the start of a year and matures at a year boundary.
3. *(Assumed)* Capital is divisible (continuous variables), no transaction costs, no taxes, no minimum ticket, no borrowing/short selling.
4. *(Assumed)* Idle (uninvested) cash earns 0 % and is carried forward to the next epoch.
5. *(Assumed)* **Only cash flows realized on or before $t=3$ count.** A B‑position that matures at $t=4$ (i.e. $k=2$) is locked past the horizon and therefore contributes nothing at $t=3$; such a choice is strictly dominated and will never be optimal.
6. *(Assumed)* Proceeds may be split arbitrarily between A, B and idle cash at each epoch (no indivisibility of the principal).

## 2. Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $T=\{0,1,2,3\}$ | — | Decision epochs (years) |
| $T_A=\{0,1,2\}$ | — | Start times at which product A can be bought (matures $t+1\le 3$) |
| $T_B=\{0,1\}$ | — | Start times at which product B can be bought (matures $t+2\le 3$) |
| $D=\{2,4\}$ | — | Admissible holding periods of B (integer multiples of 2 years) |
| $W_0$ | $100{,}000$ | Initial capital (CNY) |
| $\rho_A$ | $1.7$ | Return factor of A: 1 yuan $\to 1.7$ yuan at $t+1$ |
| $\rho_B$ | $3.0$ | Return factor of B: 1 yuan $\to 3$ yuan at maturity |
| $M$ | $500{,}000$ | Big‑M (≥ any feasible $b_t$; max reachable cash $=100{,}000\cdot1.7^3\approx491{,}513$) |

## 3. Decision variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$, $t\in T_A$ | Yuan placed in product **A** at the beginning of year $t$ (matures at $t+1$, returning $1.7\,a_t$) |
| $b_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$, $t\in T_B$ | Total yuan placed in product **B** at the beginning of year $t$ |
| $u_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$, $t\in T_B$ | Portion of $b_t$ whose B‑program matures at $t+2$, i.e. the linearization of $b_t z_{t,2}$ |
| $s_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$, $t\in\{0,1,2\}$ | Idle cash held at the end of year $t$ (0 % return), carried to $t+1$ |
| $z_{t,d}$ | $\{0,1\}$, $t\in T_B,\ d\in D$ | $=1$ iff the B‑program started at $t$ is held exactly $d$ years ($d\in\{2,4\}$) |

## 4. Objective function

$$
\boxed{\max \; W_3 \;=\; 1.7\,a_2 \;+\; 3\,u_1 \;+\; s_2}
$$

Cash at $t=3$ has exactly three sources: (i) the A‑deposit started at $t=2$ (matures $t=3$): $1.7a_2$; (ii) the B‑deposit started at $t=1$ held 2 years (matures $t=3$): $3u_1$; (iii) idle cash carried from $t=2$: $s_2$.

## 5. Constraints

**(C0) Initial budget, $t=0$**
$$a_0 + b_0 + s_0 \;=\; 100{,}000$$

**(C1) Cash balance, $t=1$** (only $a_0$ matures; B started at $t=0$ is locked)
$$a_1 + b_1 + s_1 \;=\; 1.7\,a_0 \;+\; s_0$$

**(C2) Cash balance, $t=2$** (A started at $t=1$ matures; B started at $t=0$ with $d=2$ matures; no new B can start at $t=2$ because $t+2=4>3$)
$$a_2 + s_2 \;=\; 1.7\,a_1 \;+\; 3\,u_0 \;+\; s_1$$

**(C3) One holding period per B‑program** (multiples of 2 years)
$$z_{t,2} + z_{t,4} \;=\; 1, \qquad \forall\, t\in T_B$$

**(C4–C6) Linearization of $u_t = b_t z_{t,2}$** (only the 2‑year program generates cash inside the horizon)
$$
\begin{aligned}
u_t &\le M\,z_{t,2}, &&\forall t\in T_B\\
u_t &\le b_t, &&\forall t\in T_B\\
u_t &\ge b_t - M\,(1-z_{t,2}), &&\forall t\in T_B
\end{aligned}
$$

**(C7) Domains**
$$a_t,b_t,u_t,s_t \ge 0,\qquad z_{t,d}\in\{0,1\}$$

## 6. Why the model is correct

* **Cash conservation.** (C0)–(C2) say that at every epoch all money available is split among A, B and idle cash; nothing is created or lost. The objective equals the wealth liquid at $t=3$, so maximizing it maximizes "money earned by the end of the third year".
* **Multiple‑of‑2‑years rule.** The binaries $z_{t,d}$ with $d\in\{2,4\}$ (C3) force every B‑position to be held for an integer multiple of two years; (C4)–(C6) ensure a position only pays out inside the horizon if the 2‑year option was chosen ($z_{t,4}=1 \Rightarrow u_t=0$, i.e. the money is locked until $t=4$ and is worthless at $t=3$ — never optimal, hence harmless).
* **Rolling of A.** $a_t$ is defined at every epoch, so the 1‑year deposit can be renewed year after year ($1.7\to2.89\to4.913$).
* **No unbounded variable.** Every variable appears in at least one equality or in the objective with a bounded antecedent (contrast with the candidate that used an unbounded $s_3$).

## 7. Optimal solution (verification)

Annualized: A gives $1.7$ per year; B gives $\sqrt{3}\approx1.732$ per year, and over a 2‑year block $3 > 1.7^2 = 2.89$, so **B beats A whenever it can be held to maturity inside the horizon**, and the last (third) year can only use A.

*Plan P1:* $t=0$: all $100{,}000$ into **B** (2‑year) → $t=2$: $300{,}000$ received → $t=2$: all $300{,}000$ into **A** → $t=3$: $1.7\times300{,}000 = \mathbf{510{,}000}$.

*Plan P2:* $t=0$: all $100{,}000$ into **A** → $t=1$: $170{,}000$ received → $t=1$: all $170{,}000$ into **B** (2‑year) → $t=3$: $3\times170{,}000 = \mathbf{510{,}000}$.

**Optimal value:** $W_3^{\star} = 100{,}000\times3\times1.7 = 510{,}000$ CNY (profit $=410{,}000$ CNY).

Because every yuan of initial capital can be shown to earn at most $1.7\times3 = 5.1$ by $t=3$ (A→A→A gives $4.913$, B→A gives $5.1$, A→B gives $5.1$), the model attains the upper bound $510{,}000$ and the solution is optimal. The optimum is **degenerate**: any split $x\in[0,100{,}000]$ placed in A at $t=0$ (then B at $t=1$) and $100{,}000-x$ in B at $t=0$ (then A at $t=2$) gives the same $510{,}000$.

**Model‑class remark.** Because the horizon is only 3 years, the only admissible in‑horizon duration is $2$ years, so the MILP above reduces to a pure LP if one drops the binaries and simply forbids B‑start at $t=2$; the binaries are kept because they are what enforces the "multiple of two years" rule in general and are needed as soon as a longer horizon is considered.

{"description": "Hospital nurse scheduling with regular and contract nurses.

Time periods (6 shifts of 4 hours each in a 24-hour day):
1. Shift 1: 02:00-06:00, requirement R1 = 10 nurses
2. Shift 2: 06:00-10:00, requirement R2 = 15 nurses
3. Shift 3: 10:00-14:00, requirement R3 = 25 nurses
4. Shift 4: 14:00-18:00, requirement R4 = 20 nurses
5. Shift 5: 18:00-22:00, requirement R5 = 18 nurses
6. Shift 6: 22:00-02:00, requirement R6 = 12 nurses

Nurses work in batches starting at 6 possible start times (02:00, 06:00, 10:00, 14:00, 18:00, 22:00) and work continuously for 8 hours, so each nurse covers exactly 2 consecutive 4-hour shifts.

Decision variables:
- r_i = number of REGULAR nurses starting batch at shift start time i (i = 1..6), nonnegative integer
- c_i = number of CONTRACT nurses starting batch at shift start time i (i = 1..6), nonnegative integer

Coverage: a nurse starting at batch i covers shifts i and i+1 (mod 6), since shift 6 (22:00-02:00) wraps around to shift 1 (02:00-06:00) the next day.

Coverage matrix A (6x6), where A[j][i] = 1 if a nurse starting at batch i covers shift j:
- Batch 1 (02:00) covers shifts 1, 2
- Batch 2 (06:00) covers shifts 2, 3
- Batch 3 (10:00) covers shifts 3, 4
- Batch 4 (14:00) covers shifts 4, 5
- Batch 5 (18:00) covers shifts 5, 6
- Batch 6 (22:00) covers shifts 6, 1

Objective: minimize total hourly labor cost
minimize  80 * sum_i r_i + 120 * sum_i c_i
(each nurse works 8 hours: regular $10/hr * 8 = $80; contract $15/hr * 8 = $120)

Constraints (staffing requirements, met or exceeded):
A * (r + c) >= R for each shift j = 1..6
i.e.
r1 + r6 + c1 + c6 >= 10   (shift 1: 02:00-06:00)
r1 + r2 + c1 + c2 >= 15   (shift 2: 06:00-10:00)
r2 + r3 + c2 + c3 >= 25   (shift 3: 10:00-14:00)
r3 + r4 + c3 + c4 >= 20   (shift 4: 14:00-18:00)
r4 + r5 + c4 + c5 >= 18   (shift 5: 18:00-22:00)
r5 + r6 + c5 + c6 >= 12   (shift 6: 22:00-02:00)

All r_i, c_i are nonneg integers.
